title: Grateful Dead Live at Woodstock Music  on 1969-08-16
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > analog out > Korg MR-1 DFF @ [1bit/2.8 mhz] Rate Conversion: AudioGate to [24bit/96 khz] Mastering: In WaveLab with L3 Waves Multimaximizer Rate Conversion with r8brain to [16bit/44.1 khz] > TLH > Flac

ai_review.summary: A clean sound‑board capture of Woodstock’s infamous 8/16/69 set, highlighted by a hypnotic 45‑minute “Turn On Your Lovelight” despite the show’s reputation as the Dead’s worst performance.
ai_review.review: The SBD recording is notably clear – reviewers repeatedly award it five‑star sound quality and call it an upgrade over previous versions. Musically the concert is polarising: most fans love Jerry’s soaring leads, Pigpen’s marathon Lovelight and a solid “Mama Tried,” while the brief St Stephen opener and floundering “High Time” reinforce its legend as a sloppy show.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistent praise for the recording quality (70% of reviewers give 5‑star sound ratings) and strong enthusiasm for specific songs, balanced by repeated criticism that the overall performance is one of the band’s worst.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with minimal noise; several reviewers call it a remarkable upgrade and very listenable, though a few suggest using EQ to tame occasional mud.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set starts with a painfully brief St Stephen, stumbles through “Mama Tried” and an unsteady Dark Star before settling into a marathon Lovelight that carries the show. The chaotic early half reinforces its reputation as a sloppy Woodstock performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his stinging leads, perfect tone, and overall guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for bizarre radio‑crosstalk emanating from his bass amp during the Lovelight jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Hammond organ described as beautiful, swirly, and psychedelic during the jams.
